title: Happy Chuseok
caption: Happy Chuseok from Korea. Today is the harvest moon holiday, the one day of the year most Korean families are all in the same house, and the moon tonight is the one everyone actually goes outside to look at. Koreans looking up do not see a man in the moon, they see a rabbit pounding rice cake, which is who is on the card. Wherever you are reading this from, we hope your table is full.
reply: Koreans do not see a man in the moon. They see a rabbit with a wooden mallet pounding rice cake, which is why the two on this card are busy. The image travelled here centuries ago and stuck as the picture of Chuseok. The holiday itself moves every year, the 15th day of the eighth lunar month. What do people in your country see in the full moon?
